citations.quote: Forward rates are interest rates that can be locked in today for an investment in a future time period, and are set consistently with the current term structure of discount factors
4.7 DETERMINING ZERO RATES In this section we describe a procedure known as the bootstrap method which can be used to determine zero rates
Compute the semiannual yield curve, spanning over 9 years, from the data using the bootstrap procedure

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: Curve construction inverts the pricing operation: given a vector of bond prices (deposits at the short end, futures/FRAs in the middle, par swaps at the long end), bootstrap each tenor's zero rate iteratively, then choose an interpolation rule (linear-in-zero, cubic spline, monotone cubic in log-discount factor). Small zero-rate differences amplify into large forward-rate differences.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Yield Curve Construction
